103: Number of local QP operation errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
107: Number of local protection errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
11: Shows the rate at which kilobytes are received by network adapter. The counted kilobytes include framing characters.
111: Number of local protection errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
115: Number of local CQE with errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
119: Number of local CQE with errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
123: Number of remote invalid request errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic, i.e. NAK was received indicating that the other end detected invalid OpCode request.
127: Number of remote invalid request errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
131: Number of remote access errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic, i.e. NAK was received indicating that the other end detected wrong rkey.
135: Number of remote access errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic, i.e. the local machine received RDMA request with wrong rkey.
139: Number of RNR (Receiver Not Ready) NAKs received when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
143: Number of RNR (Receiver Not Ready) NAKs sent when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
147: Number of Out of Sequence NAK received when the local machine generates outbound traffic, i.e. the number of times the local machine received NAKs indicating OOS on the receiving side.
15: Shows the number of packets received by network interface.
151: Number of Out of Sequence packet received when the local machine receives inbound traffic, i.e. the number of times the local machine received messages that are not consecutive.
155: Number of remote operation errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic, i.e. NAK was received indicating that the other end encountered an error that prevented it from completing the request.
159: Number of transport retries exceeded errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
161: Requester RNR NAK Retries Exceeded Errors
162: Requester RNR NAK Retries Exceeded Errors
163: Number of RNR (Receiver Not Ready) NAKs retries exceeded errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
171: Number of duplicate requests received when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
175: Number of timeout received when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
179: Number of packets delayed because TX ring is full.
19: Shows the rate at which packets are received by network interface.
23: Shows the number of bytes sent by network adapter. The counted bytes include framing characters.
27: Shows the rate at which kilobytes are sent by network adapter. The counted kilobytes include framing characters.
31: Shows the number of packets sent by network interface.
35: Shows the rate at which packets are sent by network interface.
39: Shows the total of bytes handled by network adapter. The counted bytes include framing characters.
43: Shows the total rate of kilobytes that are sent and received by network adapter. The counted kilobytes include framing characters.
47: Shows the total of packets handled by network interface.
51: Shows the rate at which packets are sent and received by network interface.
55: The total number of successfully received control frames.
59: Shows the number of outbound packets that could not be transmitted because of errors.
63: Shows the number of outbound packets to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent transmission. One possible reason for discarding packets could be to free up buffer space.
67: Shows the number of inbound packets that contained errors preventing them from being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
7: Shows the number of bytes received by network adapter. The counted bytes include framing characters.
71: Shows the number of inbound packets that contained error where the frame has length error. Packets received with frame length error are a subset of packets received errors.
75: Shows the number of inbound packets that contained symbol error or an invalid block. Packets received with symbol error are a subset of packets received errors.
79: Shows the number of inbound packets that contained bad CRC error. Packets received with bad CRC error are a subset of packets received errors.
83: Shows the number of inbound packets that were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol. One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.
91: Number of local length errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
95: Number of local length errors when the local machine receives inbound traffic.
99: Number of local QP operation errors when the local machine generates outbound traffic.
